sentences.text:
ORDER Petitioners in W.P.No.30506/2017 are before this Court seeking quash of the preliminary notification dated 14.06.2013 and the final notification dated 30.01.2015 in respect of the land bearing Sy.No.37/1 to an extent of 2 Acres 20 guntas situated at Aadinarayan Hosahalli Village,
Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapur Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, which was obtained from a registered deed of sale dated 03.05.1990 from their vendors.
2. That the petitioners were cultivating the said land by growing crops like Ragi, Jola, Paddy,
Vegetables and coconut.

When things stood thus, respondents-KIADB has initiated acquisition proceedings on the said land by issuing a preliminary notification, upon which the petitioner sought to NC: 2023:KHC:33715 delete the same by making a representation to the authority.

That,
respondent-authority issued a final notification, in spite the request of the petitioners for withdrawal of acquisition proceedings.
Hence, they are before this Court.

3. It is the case of the petitioners in W.P.No.24031/2016 that they are the owners of land bearing Sy.No.38/3 to an extent of 1 acre 14 guntas of land situated at Adinarayana Hosahalli Village,
Kasaba Hobli, Bangalore.
That on 30.01.2015 by final notification, the respondents-KIADB had acquired the land of the petitioners.
Being aggrieved by the same, petitioners were made representations on 26.07.2013 and 27.07.2013 to the respondents, which were not considered by respondent-KIADB.
Hence, they are before this court seeking quash of the final notification and for a further direction to the respondent-authorities to consider their representations.

4. Heard Sri. Raghavendra Kattimani, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri. Yogesh D. Naik,
learned AGA for the respondent No.1 and Sri. Basavaraj V.Sabarad, learned Senior counsel along with NC: 2023:KHC:33715 Sri. P.V.Chandrashekar, learned counsel for the respondent Nos. 2 and 3.
5.

By an affidavit dated 07.09.2022 sworn to by the petitioner No.1 in these writ petitions, it is deposed that; writ petitions are filed seeking quash of the Preliminary Notification dated 14.06.2013 and the Final Notification dated 30.01.2015.

That this Court after issuing the notice to the respondent Nos.1 to 3 on 17.10.2017 had directed the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 not to dispossess the petitioners from the subject land which is pending consideration in these petitions.
It is further deposed that during the pendency of the proceedings award notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued on 14.06.2018.

At paragraph 5 of the affidavits it is disposed that Sri. K.C. Lingegowda vs The State Of Karnataka on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34676646/

sentences.text:
during the pendency of the present writ petitions the State Legislature has brought an amendment to the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Act, 1966 with effect from 05.04.2022 by substituting certain provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and NC: 2023:KHC:33715 Transparency in Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation and Resettlement) Act, 2013 (for short 'New Act,
2013') into Section 30 of the KIAD Act, 1966.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and NC: 2023:KHC:33715 Transparency in Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation and Resettlement) Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thus, it is further deposed that in view of the amendment, petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the provisions of Section 26 of the New Act, 2013.

It is further deposed that writ petitions were filed challenging the acquisition proceedings as the nature of the lands were agricultural lands and the compensation would be of meager amount compared to the market value of the properties of the petitioners.

That in view of the changed circumstances of the petitioners getting proper and fair compensation of the new Act of 2013 such that they can purchase alternate land, the petitioners were ready to receive the compensation in accordance with provisions of Section 26 of the New Act, 2013.
It is further deposed that respondent-authorities be directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners under the provisions of the Act, 2013.
Thus, though the challenge to the acquisition was made, the relief sought in these petitions NC: 2023:KHC:33715 are restricted to seek compensation under the New Act, 2013.

6. Thus, taking note of the contents of the affidavit, this Court by order dated 29.08.2023 had observed that the applicability of amendment to Section 30 of the KIAD Act is pending consideration before the Full Bench and that the said matter is now reserved for judgment.

Thereafter, on 12.09.2023 in view of the consensus amongst the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel for the respondents that the petitioners had restricted their claim in these petitions only to the extent of compensation and further considering the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioners that there are standing fruit bearing trees and that if the respondent-authorities are permitted to utilize the lands for the purpose for which they are acquired, the same would result in changing the nature of land and would pose difficulties in computing the compensation.
Therefore, it was suggested across the Bar that a joint NC:
2023 :KHC:33715 inspection be made in the presence of the petitioners and the respondents with regard to the number and nature of the trees existing on the acquired lands.
Accordingly, on 12.09.2023 a direction was issued to conduct spot inspection in the presence of the petitioners and representatives of the respondent-KIADB on 14.09.2023 at about 11.00 a.m..
Admittedly, an inspection pursuant to the aforesaid order has been carried out in the presence of the petitioners and the representatives of the respondents.

A report of the inspection is filed today along with a memo dated 19.09.2023.
7.

Since the details with regard to extent of lands and the number of trees existing and the nature of the trees are already on record and there is no dispute with regard to the same, respondent-authorities may take into consideration of these material aspect of the matters at the time of consideration of the claim by the petitioners for compensation either under Sri.
